categories.main_business_segments: SLB operates through four primary business divisions: Digital & Integration, Reservoir Performance, Well Construction, and Production Systems. Each division addresses a distinct segment of the energy value chain, from digital solutions and asset performance to reservoir evaluation, well construction, and production systems. The company also has a growing New Energy segment focused on decarbonization, renewables, and critical minerals. Recent acquisitions, such as Aker's subsea business and the pending ChampionX transaction, further expand its portfolio.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: SLB leverages advanced digital platforms (including AI, machine learning, and cloud-based solutions like Delfi and Lumi), proprietary data analytics, and industry-leading simulators. Its production methods span subsurface characterization, well construction (including autonomous drilling), reservoir stimulation and intervention, and integrated production systems. The company also develops carbon capture, hydrogen, geothermal, and direct lithium extraction technologies, supported by a global R&D network.
categories.primary_customers_markets: SLB's primary customers are national oil companies, large integrated oil companies, and independent operators in the oil and gas sector. The company also serves customers in adjacent markets such as industrial decarbonization, renewables, and critical minerals. No single customer accounts for more than 10% of revenue, reflecting a diversified customer base across upstream, midstream, and downstream energy markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: SLB operates in more than 100 countries, with its business structured around four geographic Basins: Americas Land, Offshore Atlantic, Middle East & North Africa, and Asia. The company generates approximately 85% of its revenue from international markets, with significant operations in the Middle East & Asia, Europe & Africa, Latin America, and North America. Its global footprint is supported by regional GeoUnits tailored to local market needs.
categories.supply_chain_position: SLB primarily operates as a technology and service provider in the upstream and midstream segments of the energy supply chain, supporting exploration, development, production, and processing. Through its Production Systems division and joint ventures, it also provides equipment and solutions that extend into downstream processing and industrial applications. The company’s offerings span from subsurface to surface, pipelines, and refineries.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: SLB's strategy centers on three engines of growth: Core (oil and gas technologies), Digital (digital transformation and automation), and New Energy (decarbonization, renewables, and critical minerals). R&D priorities include digitalization, emissions reduction, carbon capture, hydrogen, geothermal, and lithium extraction. The company is committed to sustainability, with a 2050 net-zero emissions target and interim milestones for Scope 1, 2, and 3 reductions.
categories.revenue_model: SLB generates revenue primarily through the sale of services and products, including digital solutions, equipment, and integrated project management. Revenue streams include short-term service contracts, long-term construction-type contracts (recognized over time), software licensing and SaaS subscriptions, and performance-based fees (e.g., Asset Performance Solutions). In 2024, services accounted for $23.3 billion and product sales for $13.0 billion of total revenue.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: SLB faces competition from both large and small energy services and technology companies, with principal competitive factors being technological innovation, service quality, and price. Major competitors include Halliburton, Baker Hughes, and Weatherford, among others. SLB is positioned as a global technology leader with a broad, integrated portfolio and a strong emphasis on digital and sustainability-driven solutions.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, SLB reported $36.3 billion in revenue, a 10% increase year-over-year, with net income attributable to SLB of $4.5 billion. The company demonstrated strong international growth (12% year-over-year), robust cash flow from operations ($6.6 billion), and continued margin expansion. Recent acquisitions and investments in digital and new energy are expected to support further growth and portfolio resilience.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: SLB differentiates itself through its integrated technology portfolio, global scale, and leadership in digital transformation and decarbonization. The company emphasizes its ability to deliver performance improvements, cost efficiencies, and emissions reductions for customers. Its unique value proposition includes proprietary digital platforms, advanced reservoir and production technologies, and a growing suite of solutions for the energy transition.
